body: The closed flag allowlist of `viola open`: a flag outside it, or a word after `--` other than `claude`, is refused before anything starts with exit 2 — clap's usage error, plus one fixed line beside the existing dashes-pair line.

The new exit-1 refusals `terminal-not-found` and `not-live` (window left standing): each a kebab-case code word beside the unable word, with its one hint, never coloured, its fixed copy pinned by literal.
The start-against-a-holder refusals `already-live` and `stale-heartbeat`, read before any spawn, reused by `viola open`.
The `strict-modes-failed` refusal, raised before any log line or write; and no exit 11 from `viola open`.

The `--json` output of `viola open`: one document, `{"v":1,"ok":{"name","parent","window","placement"}}` on success or `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` on refusal, with no hint and no stray bytes.

The `viola --help` setup group label line, gaining `open`: `setup:  open, run, revive, verify, plugin install`; help lists served verbs only, and the two new hidden flags on `viola run` stay out of help.

The time bounds `viola open` adds: liveness wait at most 30 s, window appearance 5 s polled at 100 ms, then `unplaced`; each as a time-bound row of its own beside the full lists, falling on the driver, never on the human.
The settled 5 s compositor read bound `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` joining the a11y time-bound rows (bounds fall on the driver, never on the human) as a row of its own.

The placement outcome values recorded as codes: placed, `unplaced` (no parent window or no window seen in time), skipped off Hyprland with the seam's own `unsupported` / `unreachable` saying why; the open proceeds on a locked desktop.
The move of the new window to its parent's workspace makes no focus change: the human's focused window and keystrokes are untouched by the open.
The new log-only event kind `window {address?, workspace?, placement, origin}` and the snapshot's `window?`, replayed last line winning; logged codes-only, carrying no paths or free text.
`list --json` and MCP `list` items gain `window?` and `origin?`; the six-column human board stays as it is.
The origin (`cli` · `agent`) and the target workspace crossing onto the started `viola run`'s argv as two hidden checked flags, validated by the wrapper.
The parent defaulting to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME`; names printed in output are the parsed arguments, with control characters escaped.
The terminal argv built without any shell line, whatever characters the arguments hold; the wrapped session in its foot window keeps viola's own bytes off the terminal and run diagnostics off it.
The recorder's failure code words `move-refused`, `move-unseen` and `window-left`, asserted by tests in the code-word format with no live window.
New error types of the open path: errors as word, detail and hint; thiserror messages interpolate nothing; no stack trace or bare status as error text.
R2 is a live reading under a scratch home: it gates v2-07 but never gates CI; manual and live checks stay supplemental, the fake (a stand-in foot and a keyed clients reply) carries every CI test.

Open waits for liveness up to 30 s and for the window up to 5 s with no spinner, no elapsed-time counter, no interactive prompt and no pager; nothing announces success before the instance is confirmed live.

The terminal is resolved from PATH and spawned directly as argv elements, never through a shell, whatever characters the arguments hold; the viola it runs is the pinned absolute path, re-hashed before use.

Every name open takes — the session name, `--parent`, the parent defaulted from the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` — passes the viola name check before any path, app id or title is composed from it; the self-reported parent authenticates nothing.

Open checks the home tree by strict modes before any log opens or state is read (exit 1 `strict-modes-failed`), and reads the start collision check (`already-live`, `stale-heartbeat`) before any spawn.

New refusal and error words (`terminal-not-found`, `not-live`, the after-dashes refusal) are fixed code words; the `--json` document `{"v":1,"ok":{name,parent,window,placement}}` / `{"v":1,"error":code,"detail":null}`; refusals hold no paths, pids or ids; no exit 11; the CLI exit code rows reached.

The Hyprland seam becomes a product dependency: the product issues only the one closed move dispatch, moving only the window whose pid is its own terminal parent, with no focus change; off Hyprland the seam's own `unsupported` / `unreachable` words, no environment read.

Every compositor read is bounded by the 5 s hyprctl deadline; the window's appearance poll is bounded at 5 s (100 ms steps) then `unplaced`; open's liveness wait is bounded at 30 s then `not-live` with the window left standing — each new bound a row beside the time-bound lists.
Hyprland reply text is dropped at the parse: only the window address, workspace and pid are kept from a `clients` reply, and no reply text reaches a log, an error or an output.
A new log-only event kind `window {address?, workspace?, placement, origin}`, codes-only, its fields closed shapes validated by the shared core validators and re-checked on read.
Only the instance's wrapper writes its snapshot and start lines: the window record is the wrapper's own, never open's; the replayed `window?` is inert, runs and frames nothing, last line winning.
The origin (`cli` | `agent`) and the target workspace cross onto the started `run`'s argv as two hidden flags, checked before anything is read, as the run's lineage and launch-pair flags are.
The parent's window is read from its recorded snapshot only after the strict-modes check, else from an ancestry walk of at most 8 steps over process identity, held in memory and never recorded.
`list --json` and the MCP `list` tool items gain `window?` and `origin?`, shown only when they re-parse; the six-column human board is unchanged.
The open verb reads `VIOLA_NAME` for the parent default: a new environment read, held to the rule that a new seam or environment read needs a log entry.
The recorder's `record-move` failure codes `move-refused`, `move-unseen` and `window-left` tested over planted stubs with no live window; the test-only recorder moves only its own terminal's window.
The fake agent's stand-in `foot` and pid-keyed `clients` reply are test seams under the fake-agent feature only, compiled out of the release build.

The R2 script is test-only: a scratch home outside every repository, a private Claude config dir, nothing read or written under the operator's real Claude home, one live claude start, both windows closed on every exit path; this phase makes no live start, moves or opens no window.

body: The new CLI verb open, tested as a subprocess: its closed allowlist refused with exit 2 before anything starts, a word after `--` other than claude refused by one fixed line, the leading-slash and argv vector negatives that apply to its arguments.
No shell line is ever built from open's arguments: the terminal and the run it starts are spawned directly by argv, whatever characters the name, cwd or other arguments hold.

Open's exit codes and JSON documents: exit 1 terminal-not-found, exit 1 not-live, already-live and stale-heartbeat read before any spawn, exit 1 strict-modes-failed before any log is opened or read, no exit 11; one JSON document per run in the v1 ok/error shape with a null detail.

Human output of open and the grouped help verb table, whose setup group gains open; refusal lines are fixed literals pinned by literal asserts, with no SGR without a terminal and control characters escaped.

The new event kind window (address, workspace, placement, origin), log-only: the event line's kinds, keys and round trip, and an older reader counting it as unknown and skipping it rather than failing.

The instance snapshot gains window, written only by the wrapper (the single writer of the snapshot and its start lines, never open), and the replay from the log recovers it with the last window line winning; the replayed field set grows by it.

viola list --json items and the MCP list tool items gain window and origin; CLI and MCP keep identical payloads and the list JSON keeps mirroring the channel; the human board's six columns stay unchanged.
The wrapper's start takes two new hidden checked flags from open, origin and target workspace, on the started run's argv; a bad value is refused as a start refusal before the child.

Placement through the Hyprland seam: a bounded clients read until a window's pid is the wrapper's terminal ancestor, then the one closed move dispatch to the target workspace; no parent window gives unplaced, the seam's unsupported and unreachable skip placement with the reason recorded, no environment read for it.
The parent's window is its recorded one, else an ancestry walk of at most 8 steps held in memory; the parent defaults to the caller's VIOLA_NAME.

New time bounds (open's 30 s liveness wait, the 5 s window appearance at 100 ms polls, the 5 s compositor read bound) each land as a row of their own beside the existing time-bound lists, and tests drive them through the injected clock or a test parameter, never by sleeping, staying under the per-test kill lines.
Liveness read by open goes through the instance liveness classification (live, stale, gone) and the heartbeat staleness rules, reading the snapshot through read-or-replay.

The fake agent side gains a stand-in foot executable and a clients reply keyed to the stand-in's pid; tests reach the terminal and the compositor only through real stub executables on a test-scoped PATH, never the operator's live compositor or terminal.
The hypr tap recorder's record-move failure codes move-refused, move-unseen and window-left, each reached with no live window over a planted stub variant.
The window line and every open log line are codes-only: no session name, path, title or argument text in the logs, detail kept apart.
The claude child started through open keeps the agent identity environment strip and the child env rules of viola run; open passes no claude flag.
Spawned stand-in terminals and wrappers in tests are tied to the test (drop guard, tied spawn thread) under a test-owned home and test-owned user home; no untied viola spawn.

The R2 live reading is local only, never in CI: one real claude start under a scratch home outside every repository with a private config dir, recorded as a reading, never as verification; tests never read the host's claude sessions.
The Hyprland seam crate becomes a product dependency of the root binary: the sync-crate and tokio bans and the release-build-viola-only rule hold over the new product graph.
